retelling.text: Jesus warns His disciples to take care that their hearts do not grow heavy and dull through excess, indulgence and the worries of everyday life. Otherwise, that day could close in on them suddenly, like a snare.

That day, Jesus says, will come upon everyone on earth. So He urges them to stay alert at every moment and to keep praying, so they will have the strength to come through the trials ahead and stand before the Son of Man.

reflectionTitle: Saturday of the Thirty-Fourth Week: Keep Watch and Come, Lord Jesus
reflection: On the last Saturday of the Church's year, the readings turn our eyes toward the end and toward Christ's return.
In the First Reading, John sees a river of life flowing from God's throne and a tree whose leaves heal the nations. Night is gone, and God's servants see His face.
That is the hope we are given. Our history is moving toward healing and light, not toward chaos.
The Psalm answers with a simple prayer: "Come, Lord Jesus!" It is the cry of people who are ready to welcome Him, not afraid of Him.
Then the Gospel gives us the other side. Jesus does not describe the end to frighten us. He tells us how to be ready.
What surprises us is the danger He names. He speaks of the anxieties of daily life, not only of dramatic sin. A heart can grow drowsy simply because it is crowded with worry and busyness.
That is challenging for anyone who carries real responsibility. A full calendar and a long list of problems can quietly dull our attention to God and to the people in front of us.
Jesus's remedy is simple: stay awake and pray. Prayer is how we keep our hearts alert and steady, and it is where we find strength we do not have on our own.
At home, being awake might mean putting the phone down and truly listening to a spouse, a child or a parent. Love needs our attention before it needs our solutions.
At work, a leader who is awake notices the quiet colleague, the overwhelmed team member and the decision that affects real lives. Serving others begins with seeing them.
In our communities, vigilance means staying faithful in small, ordinary duties without waiting for a dramatic moment.
Advent begins tomorrow. Let us enter it with hearts that are clear, prayerful and ready.
We do not wait with dread. We wait for the One who wipes away every tear and gives us light that never fades.
message: Do not let worry and busyness make your heart drowsy; stay awake in prayer, and welcome the Lord who is coming with a ready heart.
